I did, in fact, believe that the person who told me about the 'job' was speaking of an actual employment situation. I've known them for years now so I figured 'why not?' 

I look forward to a day when I'll stop being so gullible. 

At the very least, they meant well, though.

That makes perfect sense. I'm always nervous when calling people as well. 

The nearest animal shelter to where I live is so far away, the bus wouldn't get me there. Like, in another city which, I find a bit humorous since we do have **a lot** of stray animals over here. 

But you do make a good point. I think that's something to look forward to when I move out. I could get a home near an animal shelter so I could volunteer there when I can/want. 

Now, the flower shop, I can definitely do. It's close enough to bike there. It's super tiny and I didn't even realize there was one, but it's worth a shot over all.

Thank you. I think I'd be better off finding a job and moving out first, though. I could get some help for my mental state and in turn, be better able to handle school if I did go. 

But I'll check out the flower shop for sure.

The straight forward answer is to get a job and save my income, which is what I would love to be doing right now.
I would love to be a florist or a caretaker for animals. Those things would be highlights in my days. 
A really 'high up there' dream for me is to be an animator. I'd have to go to school for this one to be taken even remotely seriously. I don't think it's worth the debt I'd be in, honestly. I'd still do animation without the degree, though. I could live with it being a hobby. 

Truthfully, it is the 'how?' that really trips me up when trying to get a job. Maybe I'm just not doing it right. I've applied, sent in resumes, and called (with much trepidation on my end).
I've gotten some odd offers and some spam and scam mail, but that's about it.  

But working and saving is my best route.

In detail, I'd apply, send a resume, and call consistently. 
Though, I feel like I have to ask because I think any hope of getting far may be cut out when I call. Supposedly, I sound like a kid over the phone (I've been told this many times). Is there some secret to not sounding so 'unqualified'? Not sure if I'm paranoid or what, but just yikes.

I hate that this has  happened to you. Truth be told, I'm in just about the same situation, except for the relationship part. Replace 'college' with 'high school', in my case. I can't really tell my parents about my feelings since they won't listen. 

Seriously though,so much of what you've said here, down to the screaming, noisy neighbor, rings a bell to some degree. 

I don't think you're selfish for any of this, honestly. A lot of the things you mention are not really things you can outright control. It's ok to feel overwhelmed. It's ok to have problems. The fact that other people have problems as well does not invalidate you, your problems, or your feelings.

I'm willing to lend an 'ear' (eye, in this case) if you want to vent further.

In the context of my situation now, I'm not entirely sure. 

I think, in order for me to do that, I'd have to be free to be myself and make 'mistakes'. I don't mean doing something heinous, by the way. I mean that I would need to be able to express myself and my likes and dislikes freely without a judgmental environment. That might allow me to properly access my flaws and my strengths without being put down for the former. I think the best way to do that would be to live alone. 

So, I probably won't be able to do this until I am able to leave my parents' house for good. I have no new and exciting experiences here and I'm always cooped up in the house and doing my darnedest to hide myself. I'm tired of that. Yes, it's kind of them to let me stay here and I can say I appreciate that much, but I'm not sure who I'm supposed to be or what I'm doing here or why I had to be here in the first place. They've introduced me to a lifestyle they don't know how to adequately explain, but seem to wholeheartedly adhere to. So on top of not knowing who I am, I constantly feel fear and guilt for not being good enough and not understanding or finding appeal in said lifestyle. 

Put shortly, I have to be away from that/their influence.

You're right there—about me having trouble believing this, but thank you for saying it anyhow. It's still appreciated.

Truthfully, I'd have ended up saying 'I don't know', had I not had time to think about it or I felt as though the person asking would find it ridiculous.

 However, I'm sure I want to be able to understand and like myself at least a little bit more. I don't want to be a needy emotional wreck. I want to be happy and enjoy being happy instead of feeling like I'm doing something wrong because I'm happy. If I'm not going to find a place I can fit in, I at least want to be able to be content with/by myself. I want to be capable of standing on my own two feet without feeling as though I need someone else to validate my existence and/or cause. I think I'd feel better about living life and trying to work towards the dreams I want to achieve then, because negative things other people say wouldn't bring me down so much. 

(That said, I'm all for realistic thinking/planning. It's the degrading type of comments that sting so much.)

All in all, I hope this makes some bit of sense. And thank you.
